mainTopic: How מליקה must be done: moving the סימנים behind the nape, sawing back and forth, and שמואל's rule matching מליקה to שחיטה
overview: The sons of רבי חייא taught that one may move a bird's סימנים (windpipe and food pipe) behind the עורף and then do מליקה. The גמרא proves this means moving is allowed, not required. רבי ינאי attacks them from the משנה's line 'what is valid for שחיטה is invalid for מליקה'. רבי ירמיה answers that the line excludes מוליך ומביא, sawing back and forth, and the גמרא explains that the sons of רבי חייא hold sawing is invalid in מליקה. Next, רב כהנא says the מצוה of מליקה is to cut and go down, and רבי ירמיה insists sawing is also valid, reading the words as 'this too is its מצוה'. Then שמואל teaches that what is invalid in שחיטה is also invalid in מליקה. The גמרא searches for what this excludes: not עיקור סימנין, which רמי בר יחזקאל says does not apply to birds, but a cut that starts at the slope of the head, like רב הונא's rule about שחיטה. Finally, רב אחא בריה דרבא limits רמי בר יחזקאל's rule to the view that bird שחיטה is not from the Torah, and this discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that moving the סימנים is allowed, not required
steps.stepSummary: If moving the סימנים behind the nape were required, שחיטה done that way would also be valid, so there would be no reason to mention only מליקה. So the teaching must mean moving is an extra allowance, and the משנה is talking about where nothing was moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the rule is that one must specifically move the סימנים back, why mention only pinching? Slaughtering would also work that way! So we learn that moving is only an option, and our משנה is talking about where he did not move them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves how to read the teaching of the sons of רבי חייא. Moving the סימנים behind the nape is permitted, but it is not the only way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the סימנים had to be moved first, the cut would never pass through the nape bone at all. The גמרא assumes שחיטה done that way would also be fine, so singling out מליקה would make no sense. That means the normal מליקה in the משנה cuts through the nape, and moving the סימנים is an added allowance.

keyTerms.meaning: Moves back. Here it means moving the סימנים around to behind the nape.
Specifically; only this way.
Pinching. This is the way a bird offering is killed: the כהן cuts with his fingernail from the back of the neck.
Learn from it; this proves it.
The nape, the back of the neck.

steps.whatToRemember: The sons of רבי חייא mean you MAY move the סימנים behind the nape for מליקה. The משנה's normal case is pinching straight through the nape without moving anything.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that moving [the simanim] is specifically [required],
phrases.notes: This means moving the windpipe and food pipe around to the back of the neck, as the sons of רבי חייא taught.

phrases.english: why specifically [mention] one who pinches?
Even one who slaughters [that way would be valid] too!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַף מַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it: even moving [is allowed],
and our משנה is where he did not move [them].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question raised before this section about whether the teaching of the sons of רבי חייא means 'specifically' or 'even'.
steps.raayaObject: That moving the סימנים behind the nape is an allowed option, not a requirement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the teaching mentions only מליקה and not שחיטה.

steps.title: רבי ינאי challenges the sons of רבי חייא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי cites the משנה's line that what is valid for שחיטה is invalid for מליקה. He argues it excludes moving the סימנים behind the nape, which would make that method invalid for מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: Let the young ones receive their refutation! The משנה teaches: what is valid for slaughter is invalid for pinching, and what is valid for pinching is invalid for slaughter. What does this exclude? Isn't it moving the סימנים behind the nape, teaching that this does not work for pinching?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי attacks the teaching of the sons of רבי חייא. He uses a summary line from the משנה that seems to forbid moving the סימנים for מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line 'valid for שחיטה, invalid for מליקה' must be excluding some case. רבי ינאי suggests that case is moving the סימנים behind the nape: it works for שחיטה but not for מליקה. If so, the משנה contradicts the sons of רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: Young men. Here it refers to the sons of רבי חייא.
Here it means a refutation, an answer that knocks down their view.
To exclude what? It asks what case a line in the text comes to leave out.
Valid / invalid.
Slaughter with a knife across the throat.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
Let the young ones receive their refutation,
phrases.notes: 'The young ones' is his way of calling the sons of רבי חייא.

phrases.english: for it is taught:
It turns out: what is valid for slaughter is invalid for pinching,
[and what is] valid for pinching is invalid for slaughter.
To exclude what?
Is it not to exclude one who moves the simanim
behind the nape, that [this is] not [valid for pinching]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the teaching of the sons of רבי חייא is clear, רבי ינאי challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching of the sons of רבי חייא that one may move the סימנים behind the nape for מליקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's line must exclude something. The natural candidate is moving the סימנים, which would make it invalid for מליקה.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: the line excludes a tooth and fingernail
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה defends the sons of רבי חייא. He says the line excludes a tooth or fingernail, which are fine for מליקה but not for שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: No, the line comes to exclude a tooth and a fingernail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה pushes off רבי ינאי's attack. He offers a different case that the משנה's line could be excluding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the line refers to a tooth and fingernail, it says nothing about moving the סימנים. Then the sons of רבי חייא are safe. A fingernail works for מליקה, but slaughtering with an attached tooth or nail is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: A tooth and a fingernail, still attached to the body.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: לָא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said: No,
[it comes] to exclude a tooth and a fingernail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ינאי's reading of what the line excludes.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי ינאי's claim that the line must refer to moving the simanim.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Another case, a tooth and fingernail, could be what the line excludes.

steps.title: Tooth and fingernail are already stated openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבה בר בר חנה's answer. The case of a tooth and fingernail is already taught openly, so this line is not needed for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a tooth and a fingernail are taught openly already!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבה בר בר חנה's answer, so the challenge of רבי ינאי comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה already says plainly that slaughtering with a tooth or fingernail is invalid. A summary line would not be needed just to repeat that. So the line must be excluding something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, in so many words.

phrases.english: Tooth and fingernail, [the תנא] teaches them openly.
phrases.notes: An earlier משנה (חולין 15b) already lists tooth and fingernail as invalid for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר בר חנה's claim that the line excludes a tooth and fingernail.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something stated openly elsewhere would not be repeated in a summary line.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the line excludes sawing back and forth
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה offers a new answer. The line excludes מוליך ומביא, cutting by moving back and forth, which is fine for שחיטה but not for מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי ירמיה said: it comes to exclude drawing back and forth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a new answer to defend the sons of רבי חייא. He says the line excludes sawing back and forth during מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שחיטה the knife is supposed to move back and forth. In מליקה the כהן must press and cut in one motion. So 'valid for שחיטה, invalid for מליקה' can refer to sawing, not to moving the סימנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving forward and back. This means cutting with a sawing motion.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yirmeya said:
[it comes] to exclude drawing back and forth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of רבה בר בר חנה with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line excludes moving the סימנים (רבי ינאי), or a tooth and fingernail (רבה בר בר חנה).
steps.terutzMaskana: The line excludes sawing back and forth in מליקה, so it does not contradict the sons of רבי חייא.

steps.title: But what about the view that sawing is valid in מליקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבי ירמיה's answer works only for the view that sawing in מליקה is invalid. What would the view that it is valid say?
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for the one who says drawing back and forth in pinching is invalid. But for the one who says it is valid, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה's answer. It only works according to one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute about whether sawing back and forth is allowed in מליקה. If it is allowed, the line cannot be excluding it. Then we are back to needing a case to exclude, and moving the סימנים returns as the candidate.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well; it fits.
What is there to say? It points out a problem for another opinion.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
drawing back and forth in pinching is invalid,
but according to the one who says [it is] valid,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's answer that the line excludes sawing back and forth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that sawing is valid in מליקה, the line cannot be excluding it. So the problem from רבי ינאי comes back.

steps.title: The sons of רבי חייא hold that sawing is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the sons of רבי חייא themselves hold that sawing back and forth in מליקה is invalid. So for them, רבי ירמיה's answer works and their teaching stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי חייא hold like the one who says drawing back and forth in pinching is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question. The sons of רבי חייא follow the opinion that sawing in מליקה is invalid, so the משנה's line can exclude sawing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We only need to defend the sons of רבי חייא by their own opinion. Since they hold sawing is invalid in מליקה, the line excludes sawing according to them. It no longer has to exclude moving the סימנים, so רבי ינאי's attack is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold like the one who says. It ties a person to one side of a dispute.

steps.whatToRemember: The line 'valid for שחיטה, invalid for מליקה' excludes sawing back and forth, not moving the סימנים. So the sons of רבי חייא's permission to move the סימנים behind the nape for מליקה stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the teaching that the סימנים may be moved behind the nape for מליקה. It also shows that the sons of רבי חייא hold sawing back and forth is invalid in מליקה.

phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Chiyya hold

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא בִּמְלִיקָה – פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: like the one who says drawing back and forth in pinching is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question against רבי ירמיה's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the defense to the opinion of the people being defended
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ירמיה's answer fails for the opinion that sawing is valid, so the sons of רבי חייא seem exposed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sons of רבי חייא hold that sawing is invalid, so for them the line excludes sawing and their teaching stands.

steps.title: רב כהנא: The proper way to do pinching is to cut and go down
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא teaches that the מצוה of מליקה is to cut and move downward, and calls this 'its מצוה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The מצוה of pinching is to cut and go downward, and this is its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב כהנא about how מליקה should be done: the כהן cuts with his fingernail and keeps moving downward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps asked whether sawing back and forth is allowed in מליקה. רב כהנא now describes the proper way: one cut that moves straight down. The words 'this is its מצוה' sound exclusive, and the next steps argue over that.

keyTerms.meaning: Pinching: cutting a bird offering's neck from the back with the כהן's fingernail
Cuts and goes down: cutting in one downward direction
Its מצוה: the proper way to do it

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
The מצוה of pinching: one cuts and continues downward,
and this is its מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מִצְוַת מְלִיקָה קוֹצֵץ וְיוֹרֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new teaching about how מליקה is done, which ties into the earlier question about sawing back and forth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The proper way to do מליקה is to cut and go downward.

steps.title: רבי אבין reads this as ruling out back-and-forth cutting
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין first thought that רב כהנא meant only cutting downward is allowed, and back and forth is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין thought to say: Cutting and going down, yes. Moving back and forth, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין makes an inference from רב כהנא's words: since he said 'this is its מצוה,' cutting back and forth must be invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין reads 'this is its מצוה' as meaning 'only this.' So in his reading, מוליך ומביא would be ruled out for מליקה. The word סבר hints that this first reading is about to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say: a first understanding that is often rejected
Moving back and forth, like sawing
Yes / no

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin thought to say:
Cuts and continues downward, yes;
draws back and forth, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes an inference from רב כהנא's wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי אבין's first reading, only cutting downward is valid in מליקה, not back and forth.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: Back-and-forth cutting is surely valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rejects רבי אבין's reading and says back-and-forth cutting is valid in מליקה, 'all the more so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to him: All the more so, moving back and forth in pinching is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tells רבי אבין that his inference is wrong: cutting back and forth is certainly valid for מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All the more so' means back and forth is even more obviously valid than cutting straight down. Moving back and forth is the normal valid way of cutting in שחיטה. If even straight-down cutting is allowed in מליקה, back and forth is surely allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so: this case is even more obvious
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: In step 5, רבי ירמיה explained the view that back and forth is invalid in מליקה, and steps 6-7 showed this is a dispute. Here he gives the other view, that back and forth is valid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him:
All the more so that drawing back and forth
in pinching is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אבין's inference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אבין's reading that back-and-forth cutting is invalid in מליקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Back-and-forth cutting is, if anything, more clearly valid than cutting straight down.

steps.title: Then why say 'this is its מצוה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if back and forth is valid, what do רב כהנא's words 'this is its מצוה' mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'this is its מצוה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה. The words 'this is its מצוה' sound like only cutting downward is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין's reading came straight from these words. If רבי ירמיה is right, the wording seems to say too much. The גמרא needs to explain the phrase in a new way.

keyTerms.meaning: And what: asks what a phrase means

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of 'this is its מצוה'?
phrases.notes: The phrase sounds like it means 'only this way,' and that is the problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ירמיה's position from the wording of רב כהנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that back and forth is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'This is its מצוה' seems to make cutting downward the only valid way.

steps.title: Read it as 'this too is its מצוה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: read רב כהנא as saying 'this TOO is its מצוה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: This too is its מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב כהנא's words should be understood as 'this too is a proper way,' not 'only this way.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the word 'too' (אף) changes the meaning. Cutting downward is one valid way, and back and forth is still valid. So רבי ירמיה's view fits רב כהנא's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Say: read the words this way
Also, too

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ירמיה, both cutting downward and moving back and forth are valid ways to do מליקה.

phrases.english: Say: That too is its מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'This is its מצוה' means only cutting downward is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means cutting downward is also a valid way, so back and forth stays valid.

steps.title: שמואל: What is valid or invalid in slaughter matches pinching
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes שמואל: any place valid for שחיטה is valid at the matching spot on the back of the neck for מליקה, and anything invalid in שחיטה is invalid in מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of שמואל: Anything valid in slaughter, the matching spot on the nape is valid in pinching. So something invalid in slaughter is invalid in pinching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section with a general rule from שמואל linking שחיטה and מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה cuts the front of the neck, and מליקה cuts from the back. שמואל says the valid zone on the front sets the valid zone on the back. The second half, about what is invalid, is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher slaughter, cutting the throat from the front
Opposite it, the matching spot
The back of the neck, the nape
Invalid

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Shmuel said:
Any place that is valid for slaughter
is correspondingly valid on the nape for pinching,
which implies: what is invalid for slaughter
is invalid for pinching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל הַכָּשֵׁר בִּשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, a general rule comparing שחיטה and מליקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The valid and invalid areas for מליקה match those of שחיטה, on the back of the neck.

steps.title: What does this rule come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the 'invalid in שחיטה, invalid in מליקה' part comes to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical case שמואל's rule is meant to rule out. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes שמואל's words teach something new. It now looks for the specific case that is invalid in מליקה because it is invalid in שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what? What case does this rule out?

phrases.english: What does this serve to exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what שמואל's rule rules out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is invalid in מליקה because it is invalid in שחיטה.

steps.title: It cannot be ripping out the סימנים, which doesn't apply to birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the rule excludes עיקור סימנין but rejects this, because רמי בר יחזקאל taught there is no עיקור disqualification for birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it excludes ripping the סימנים, didn't רמי בר יחזקאל teach: there is no ripping of סימנים in a bird!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer, ripping the סימנים out of place, and right away knocks it down with a teaching of רמי בר יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עיקור סימנין makes an animal's שחיטה invalid. But רמי בר יחזקאל taught that this disqualification does not apply to birds. So שמואל's rule, which is about birds in מליקה, cannot be teaching it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
Ripping the windpipe and food pipe out of place before cutting them
But isn't it so: introduces a challenge
A bird

phrases.english: If we say it serves to exclude ripping the simanim,
but didn't Rami bar Yechezkel teach:
There is no disqualification of ripping the simanim in a bird!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְמַעוֹטֵי עִיקּוּר סִימָנִין, וְהָא תָּנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests and rejects a first answer to 'what does it exclude.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that שמואל's rule excludes עיקור סימנין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עיקור סימנין does not disqualify a bird at all.

steps.title: רב פפא: The rule excludes the head
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says שמואל's rule excludes doing מליקה at the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: To exclude its head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new answer: שמואל's rule teaches that cutting at the head is invalid in מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The head is outside the valid zone for שחיטה. By שמואל's rule, the matching spot is outside the valid zone for מליקה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Its head

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It serves to exclude its head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after the first one was rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule excludes doing מליקה at the head.

steps.title: The head is obvious: the verse says 'by its nape'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that excluding the head is obvious, since the פסוק says 'ממול ערפו,' by its nape, and not at its head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its head is obvious! The Torah said 'adjacent to its nape,' and not at its head!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: we do not need שמואל's rule to rule out the head, because the פסוק already does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the מליקה is done 'ממול ערפו,' by the nape. The head clearly is not the nape. So רב פפא's answer seems to give שמואל's rule nothing new to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious: why would we need to be told this?
Adjacent to its nape, the place for מליקה
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Its head, isn't that obvious?
The Merciful One said: "Adjacent to its nape,"
and not at its head!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the rule excludes the head.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק already rules out the head, so שמואל's rule would add nothing.

steps.title: 'Head' means the slope of the head, sliding down into place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'head' means the slope of the head: someone started cutting there, went past the valid area, and kept going down until he reached the right place.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'its head'? The slope of its head. For example, he started at the slope of its head, went beyond the proper area, and kept going until he reached below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב פפא did not mean a cut done fully at the head. He meant a cut that began at the slope of the head and slid down into the valid zone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of this cut ends up in the right place, so we might think it is valid. שמואל's rule teaches that it is invalid, just as it would be in שחיטה. So the rule does teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: The slope of its head, where the head slants into the neck
Went beyond the proper area of the cut, toward the head
Below: down to the proper place
For example

phrases.english: What is "its head"?
The slope of its head,
for example, where he began at the slope of its head
and went beyond the proper area and continued
until he reached below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing what 'head' means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Head' means cutting fully at the head, which the פסוק already rules out.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Head' means a cut that began at the slope of the head and slid down into the proper area. That cut is invalid.

steps.title: This matches רב הונא's ruling: a third cut too high makes it invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this fits רב הונא in the name of רב אסי: if someone cut a third too high and two-thirds in the right place, the שחיטה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like what רב הונא said in the name of רב אסי: If he went too high for one-third and slaughtered two-thirds properly, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its explanation with a similar ruling about שחיטה from רב הונא in the name of רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שחיטה, a cut that starts too high is invalid even if most of it is in the right place. By שמואל's rule, the same is true in מליקה. That is exactly the case of starting at the slope of the head.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is like: links to another teaching
One-third
Invalid, describing the slaughtered animal

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule teaches that a מליקה cut which starts at the slope of the head is invalid, even if it ends in the right place. This matches the שחיטה law of רב הונא in the name of רב אסי.

phrases.english: And this is like what Rav Huna said in the name of Rav Asi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: for Rav Huna said that Rav Asi said:
If he went beyond the proper area for one-third
phrases.notes: This is about שחיטה: he cut the first third of the windpipe too high, above the proper area.

phrases.english: and slaughtered two-thirds in the proper place, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation of 'head' with a parallel ruling about שחיטה.
steps.raayaObject: That a מליקה cut starting at the slope of the head is invalid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא in the name of רב אסי: a שחיטה with one-third cut too high and two-thirds in place is invalid.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל's rule only fits one opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא tells רב אשי that the rule 'there is no עיקור סימנין in a bird' only applies according to the view that bird שחיטה is not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: The teaching of רמי בר יחזקאל, that ripping out the סימנין does not disqualify a bird, only works for the person who holds that שחיטה of a bird is not required by the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא puts a limit on the rule of רמי בר יחזקאל that the גמרא used back in step 15. He is setting up the next move, which will look at the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, it sounded like 'no עיקור for birds' was true for everyone. Now we learn it depends on a bigger argument: whether bird שחיטה comes from the Torah. If it does not, the rules of עיקור may not apply to birds; but according to the other opinion, the rule might be different.

keyTerms.meaning: Ripping or tearing the windpipe and foodpipe out of place, instead of cutting them properly
The two 'signs' cut in שחיטה: the windpipe and the foodpipe
'We only said this...': a phrase that limits a rule to a certain case
'The one who says': refers to a certain opinion in an argument
Whether slaughtering a bird is required by the Torah itself

steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching. It only says his teaching fits one side of an argument about bird שחיטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer in step 15 depended on רמי בר יחזקאל's rule. If that rule only works for one opinion, the earlier answer may need another look.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
That which Rami bar Yechezkel teaches,
phrases.notes: This is the same teaching the גמרא quoted back in step 15.

phrases.english: "There is no disqualification of ripping the simanim in a bird,"
we said it only

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין שְׁחִיטָה לָעוֹף מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: according to the one who says there is no slaughtering for a bird from the Torah,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the source used in step 15 and limits it to one opinion about bird שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that there is no עיקור סימנין disqualification for birds only applies according to the view that bird שחיטה is not from the Torah.
